system_prompt:
You are a medical pathology simplification assistant. Convert the following surgical pathology diagnostic report into simple, plain English that a patient and their family can understand (at a 6th-grade reading level).

=== EXTRACTED CLINICAL ENTITIES — YOU MUST RETAIN ALL OF THESE ===
Specimen: Prostate; Prostatectomy
  Associated structure: bilateral seminal vesicles
  Associated structure: bilateral ductus deferentes
Histologic diagnosis: Acinar adenocarcinoma (bilateral)
  ICD-O-3: 8140/3
Gleason Score: 4 + 3 = 7 (7b) | ISUP Grade Group: 3 | High-grade pattern: 70%
Invasion status: Perineural invasion: present; Lymphovascular invasion: absent; Extracapsular extension: present; Seminal vesicle invasion: present
Resection status: R1
  Margin — apical: negative
  Margin — ductus deferentes (bilateral): negative
  Margin — basal (ventral and dorsal) right and left: positive (19 mm)
IHC markers:
  • CK AE1/3: positive — marks the tumor cells
  • AMACR: focal overexpression — supports diagnosis of adenocarcinoma
  • MA903: negative — no expression
  • p63: negative — no expression
Additional finding: Tertiary grade 5 (5% proportion)
Additional finding: Gleason pattern 4 proportion: 70%
Additional finding: Gleason pattern 3 proportion: 25%
Additional finding: Immunohistochemical staining not performed in the border area for technical reasons
Additional finding: TNM classification: pT3b, pN0(0/9), L0, V0, Pn1, R1
=================================================================
CRITICAL RETENTION RULE: Every entity, value, measurement, date, medication name, finding, and recommendation listed above MUST appear in your simplified output. Do not omit any of them.

Rules:
1. Explain what tissue or organ was examined (e.g. prostate specimen removed during surgery).
2. Keep essential medical terms but immediately explain each in parentheses on first use, e.g. 'adenocarcinoma (a cancer that starts in the gland cells of an organ)'.
3. Explain the cancer type, whether it is localized or spreading, and the grade in plain words:
   - Explain Gleason score simply: e.g. 'Gleason score 7 (a grading system from 6 to 10 that shows how abnormal the cells look; 7 means moderately aggressive cells)'.
   - Explain surgical margins simply: e.g. 'resection margins (the outer cut edge of the tissue removed by the surgeon; clear/R0 margins mean no cancer cells were touching the edge)'.
   - Explain IHC stains simply: e.g. 'immunohistochemistry (special chemical dye tests that identify specific proteins in cancer cells)'.
4. Preserve all measurements (weights, dimensions in cm or mm, percentages) accurately. Never fabricate or omit numbers.
5. Write as continuous plain prose paragraphs without bullet points or headers.
6. Maintain a calm, objective, and supportive tone. Do not provide speculative prognoses or medical advice beyond what is written in the report.
7. Output only the simplified text, nothing else.
8. CRITICAL — ENTITY RETENTION: Every entity listed in the extracted entities block above MUST appear in your simplified output — including specimen weight, dimensions, Gleason score primary + secondary + total + ISUP Grade Group, percentage of high-grade pattern, every margin location and its status, every IHC marker and its result, and invasion findings. Do not omit any of them.

output_text:
The doctor removed your prostate gland during surgery, along with the seminal vesicles (the glands that make fluid for semen) and the ductus deferentes (the tubes that carry sperm) on both sides of your body. The lab examined this tissue and found a type of cancer called acinar adenocarcinoma (a cancer that starts in the gland cells of an organ) in both sides of the prostate. This specific type of cancer is identified by the code 8140/3.

To understand how aggressive the cancer is, the pathologist used a grading system called the Gleason score, which ranges from 6 to 10. Your score is 4 + 3 = 7, specifically labeled as 7b. This places your cancer in ISUP Grade Group 3, which means the cells are moderately aggressive. The report breaks down the cell types: 70% of the cancer cells are the more aggressive pattern 4 type, 25% are the less aggressive pattern 3 type, and a small portion, 5%, is a very aggressive pattern 5 type known as tertiary grade 5.

The report also shows that the cancer has spread beyond the main prostate gland. It has grown into the tissue outside the prostate, a condition called extracapsular extension. It has also invaded the seminal vesicles on both sides. Additionally, the cancer cells were found traveling along the nerves, which is called perineural invasion. However, the cancer was not found in the lymph vessels, so lymphovascular invasion is absent.

The surgeon checked the edges of the removed tissue, known as resection margins, to see if any cancer cells were left behind. A clear margin means no cancer was touching the cut edge. In your case, the top edge (apical margin) was clear, and the edges of the ductus deferentes on both sides were also clear. However, the bottom edge (basal margin) on both the right and left sides, including the front (ventral) and back (dorsal) parts, had cancer cells touching the cut edge. This area of cancer at the edge measured 19 mm. Because cancer was found at the edge, the surgery is classified as R1, meaning some microscopic cancer cells may remain in the body.

To confirm the diagnosis, the lab used immunohistochemistry (special chemical dye tests that identify specific proteins in cancer cells). The test for CK AE1/3 was positive, which marks the tumor cells. The test for AMACR showed focal overexpression, which supports the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. The tests for MA903 and p63 were negative, meaning those proteins were not expressed. The lab noted that they could not perform the staining in the border area for technical reasons.

Finally, the overall stage of the cancer is described using the TNM classification system. Your stage is pT3b, which means the cancer has spread to the seminal vesicles. pN0(0/9) means that out of 9 lymph nodes checked, none had cancer. L0 and V0 mean no cancer was found in lymph or blood vessels. Pn1 indicates the presence of perineural invasion. The final resection status is R1, confirming that cancer cells were present at the surgical margin.
